dengi: Polari's money is minted in gold, silver, and copper, with fixed ratios between denominations. The coins' names refer to the Empire's symbols and its holy Foremothers . Coins From the highest denomination to the lowest: Hilt — a gold coin, or a “gold piece.” It bears an image of the grip of the Eternal Hilt , which gives it its name. Its sheen is “yellow with a glint of gold,” so thieves call hilts “yellowboys.” A hilt = 4 elenas = 32 glorias = 256 agatkas: a pilgrim could feed himself for two months on one. Large sums, wages, and the prices of Objects are reckoned in hilts. Harmon, for example, hoped to sell the Radiant Sphere for at least thirty thousand hilts, while a kair's pay was five gold pieces a month. They are worn on the robes of the priestess of her order, and the "Wings of Miriam" are referred to as her Subject. Traditionally, only the Lands of the Crown paid the Dynasty's permanent tax. ( Crownlands ) The great Houses, rulers of counties and duchies, were indebted to the Crown for military service and other vassalage services, but not for filing. The tax was paid only by those who wanted to pay off the service, and there were few of them. Adrian, on the other hand, dreamed of connecting the entire empire with rails, and this required many times more gold than the Crown had. The only conceivable source Erwin called to file with the Great Houses: the vassal service for all lands should be abolished and replaced by a tax. vozdushnyj-shar: The balloon , or heavenly ship, is an invention of the Laemian master-hypothecist Hortense. ( Hortensius ) It was bought and improved by Harmon Paula , and then from memory built a new ball in the service of the Origins. Horam, who called the invention a ball, Hortensius corrected: “This is not a ball, glorious master! This is a heavenly ship designed to plow sky-high!” In "The Skyship and the Girl" Hortensius invented the ball about a year before August 1774. He noticed that a piece of paper thrown into the fire took off first. Then the master put the bag on the furnace pipe, weighed it and estimated how much hot air will lift a person. But the ship came out “an extremely stupid means of transportation”: barely lifted two, there was frost at the top, and the ball flew only “where the wind blows”. dom-almera: Description The Almeras are one of the Empire's Great Houses , descended from Agatha the Radiant. They ruled the richest duchy in Polaris, the Red Land. In the number of Sacred Objects held by the house, Almera was second only to the Illustrious Dynasty: the Almeras had one hundred and twenty Objects, while the Dynasty had more than three hundred. On the Day of the Descent, the dukes sometimes displayed part of their ancestral collection in Aleridan's central square for the townspeople's enjoyment. The house's coat of arms and cloaks bear a tower and a sun. Joaquin remarked that the sun setting behind Evergard's tower looked exactly like the ancestral coat of arms. At the summer games of 1774, Almera's knights wore white and gold. In a scene set in 1756, Duke Aiden is described riding a white horse, dressed in snowy white with a golden coat of arms, beside the “bicoloured” Desmond Origin. According to Lady Karen in the collector's edition of Arrow, Coin, Spark , only Almeran nobles are admitted to the Almeran guard: they are considered more firmly attached to their land and better acquainted with the laws of honour. According to the Guide to the Lands of Polari, Almera has fully pr
dom-farvej: Description The Farways were counts, the foremost vassals of House Lightheart . After the Jesters' Conspiracy , the Lighthearts lost power, and Emperor Tellurian granted Hope to Henry Farway , choosing him over Count Flame. The Farways were therefore considered new dukes: they had ruled for only around twenty years, while their vassals still remembered the Lighthearts' rule, and the Flames sympathised with the fallen family. Almost all Farways belong to Foremother Elena's lineage. Land and Wealth According to the Guide to the Lands of Polari, Hope 's largest cities are Heart of Light, Farway, and Leongard. Heart of Light, surrounded by three rings of fortifications, is reputed to be the Empire's best-defended fortress. A railway connects Farway to Heart of Light, from which trains also run to Labelin. Gold and copper mines underpin the economy; there are also two spark workshops, textile factories, and stud farms. The Guide notes that House Farway, having recently come to power, is developing industry but expends too much effort keeping its vassals, the Lighthearts and Flames, obedient, resulting in stagnation. Hope also competes fiercely with Almera: for years, the late Aiden Alme
dom-labelin: Overview House Labelin is a Great House descended from Foremother Sophia. According to the Guide to the Lands of Polari, Sophia the Majestic is the patroness of the Southern Way , Foremother of the family hearth, care, and maternal love. Her veneration is evident in southern daily life: at Marquess Doyle's feast, when Magda's army approached Doyle, “Sophia was praised three times as often as Yanmei.” The house rules the Southern Way, through which the main trade route runs from the Crownlands and Shimmery to the North. Its tolls and markups brought the Labelins fabulous wealth. According to the Guide, the duchy's merchant fleet numbers around 1200 vessels and is the largest in the Empire. Duke Maurice himself boasted to Erwin that his fleet was “many times stronger” than the northern one. The Origins possessed eighty-seven Sacred Objects , while the Labelins, according to Vittor Shayland, had around sixty. Maurice sought to close the gap through purchases. In the summer of 1774, the duke himself said that his collection contained seventy Objects. Coat of Arms and Colours The soldiers of the Southern Way wore caftans embroidered with Labelin's arms: blue dolphins and golden sheaves
dom-lajthart: House Lightheart is a former Great House that ruled the Duchy of Hope until the Jesters' Conspiracy . At the beginning of the series, all that remains of the once-powerful family is the last duke's daughter Karen and his youngest son Edgar , who changed his surname to Flame, together with Edgar's children. Description The Lighthearts descended from Foremother Elena . The lineage was considered exceedingly ancient: Humans and Gods says Karen belonged to a house “more ancient than Farway and Labelin, than even the Illustrious Dynasty itself,” and was “probably the most highborn noblewoman” at court. The Guide to the Lands of Polari identifies endurance, good fortune, and pride as the Great House of Lightheart's defining traits. According to the Guide, the Farways who succeeded them are better known for caution and skilful manoeuvring. The house's capital was Heart of Light , the strongest fortress in the Empire. The Lighthearts also personally owned Leongard, “Hope's gateway to the sea.” According to Karen in the collector's edition of Arrow, Coin, Spark , Leongard in those days was the Far Sea's largest port and a junction on the Golden Route from Shimmery to the Crown. The finance
dom-litlend: Overview House Litland is one of the Great Houses of the Empire of Polari. It rules the Duchy of Litland on the continent's eastern coast, south of Mason's Bay. The Litlands trace their ancestry to Foremother Yanmei and take pride in it: “We are of Yanmei's lineage!” Yet Litland particularly venerates Foremother Susan, the guardian of health. When the wounded in Melorange began recovering, the townspeople boasted, “Foremother Susan has paid us a visit!” The ancestral seat is Bessifor Castle, with its famous library, supposedly the finest in the South. The duchy's capital is Melorange , a city of two hundred thousand. The house sends two representatives to the Chamber . According to Rebecca , every Litland has an “obsession.” Her mother adores children, her uncle books and spiders, her father loves asking for advice, and Becca herself is obsessed with horses. Land and People According to the Guide to the Lands of Polari, “Litland” means “little land,” although the duchy is comparable in area to Almera or Darkwater. The first settlers considered only the strip of meadows in the Hollywell floodplain habitable and were so afraid of the jungle that they would not settle anywhere within
dom-nortvud: Overview The Northwoods are one of the Empire of Polari's Great Houses and rulers of the northern County of Northwood . According to Erwin Origin , the land is ruled by descendants of free archers and northern pirates, and the Northwood people bowed to the Dynasty “only recently, less than two centuries ago.” The house traces its ancestry to Foremother Susan, to whom the Northwood people pray and by whose name they swear: “Glory to Susan!” Susan is the seventh Foremother: “Seven. The seventh Foremother, Susan,” Navi whispered to Sybil after she lost her memory. The Northwoods pride themselves on their freedom but must keep an eye on their powerful neighbour, House Origin . All her life, Sybil jealously competed with the Origins over lavish meals and luxurious clothes; Erwin thought the difference lay not in wealth or the number of swords, but in faith: the Origins believed in their own greatness, whereas Sybil did not. As Mira saw it, the Empire regarded Northwood as “a primeval forest full of bears and bearded boors.” Symbols and Customs The bear. Northwood's sacred animal and symbol of its strength; the Northwood people themselves are called “bears.” The house's arms show a bear
dom-oridzhin: Overview The Origins are one of the Great Houses of the Empire of Polari, rulers of the northern Duchy of Origin, whose capital is First Winter . The full names of members of the house include the formula “of the lineage of Agatha”: the Origins regard themselves as descendants of Foremother Agatha the Radiant, the “grandchildren of Agatha”. In the North, it is believed that they inherited their pride, perceptiveness, and a measure of the gift of foresight from her. Local legend also links the house to Agatha herself: in the Roe Deer Grotto above First Winter, the Foremother is said to have milked a goat and given its milk to the first duke. The Cathedral of Agatha the Radiant in First Winter, built, according to Vittor Shayland, by the legendary Lord Reidan nine hundred years ago, is described as “as old as House Origin itself”. The northerners and their armies are called Agathans after the Foremother, and their battle cry is “Glory to Agatha!” The house's coat of arms depicts a black bat with an arrow in its claws. According to the “Guide to the Lands of Polari”, the dynasty's founder, Reidan Adler, chose a little bird capable of catching an arrow in flight as his emblem, symbolis
dom-shejland: History The Old Counts About three centuries ago, a knight received from the emperor an immense, deserted region north of Smoky Distance , a rectangle two hundred miles from east to west and four hundred from south to north, reaching all the way to the Sea of Ice , together with the title of Count of Shayland. No one wanted the misty land, which was said to be full of monsters. The count chose his own coat of arms: a signal horn, the instrument of scouts in the imperial army of the day, entwined with ivy, the symbol of the misty land where ivy grew everywhere. For a century and a half, the counts ruled reasonably well: they built towns and castles, granted generous plots of land to peasants, and established a fleet on the lake and the Torrey . The county grew rich on brightly dyed linen, for which silver from Almera and the Southern Way flowed north. Its wealth attracted its neighbours. Year after year, the Northwooders from the east and nomads from the west sliced land away from Shayland. In the end, all that remained of the county was a strip forty miles wide, twenty miles on either bank of the Torrey, and four hundred miles long, from the lake to the sea (sixteen and a hundred a
dom-yanmej: Overview Polari's imperial dynasty, the “Illustrious Dynasty,” traces its descent from Foremother Yanmei the Merciful. A saying runs: “Yanmeians are born to rule, Agathans to fight, Sophians to care for others.” The lineage of Yanmei includes not only the ruling family but many other nobles, such as Baronet Ember and Viscount Shellier ; however, only those entered in the Dynasty's genealogy have a claim to the throne. Dimples are repeatedly described as a distinguishing feature of Yanmeians. The sovereign rules the Crownlands directly, while in the other lands the sovereign's laws are ratified by the Chamber of Representatives . The symbols of authority are the Eternal Hilt , a transparent sacred dagger handed to each new sovereign and unsheathed at the coronation; the Star Crown, with its blue diamond; and the Glove of Might, or Yanmei's Glove. The Dynasty also owned other Sacred Objects , kept in the Imperial Citadel. The imperial house is protected by the Azure and Scarlet Guards. Yanmei's diaries serve as guidance for rulers. Three Inaccurate Names According to the Guide to the Lands of Polari, the ruling house is called the Illustrious, Arden, and Yanmei Dynasty, but essential
grei: Who Are the Greys? A grey is a warrior in the service of a kair , a northern knight of House Origin . Greys are distinguished by their grey cloaks: on the battlefield, kairs are recognised by their red-and-black cloaks and greys by their grey ones. After the capture of Doyle in Only One Star, the fallen northerners were covered with their own cloaks: black for the kairs, grey for the greys. Each kair is usually accompanied by two greys, though some have three. In Arrow, Coin, Spark, Erwin explains to the mechanic Louis that a grey is not a squire. A southern knight's squire is his assistant and comrade-in-arms; he hunts and feasts as his master's equal, and sometimes even enters a tournament. A grey is “beneath knightly amusements.” Outside battle, his only duties are to improve his skills and serve his master. A kair gives his grey any dirty, troublesome, or exhausting task, and a grey is punished severely for arguing or neglecting his duties. Erwin's conclusion is that “a grey is his master's dog.” Under northern law, a kair has absolute authority over his grey. When Erwin intervened in the punishment of Kair Jemis's wounded grey, Captain Theobart reminded him: “My vassal's vassa
kajry: The Rank of Kair A kair is a warrior-knight of the northern duchy of Origin . The rank is conferred through initiation: a lord touches the warrior's shoulder with a sword, and the warrior swears to honour the precepts of the Foremothers and the laws of martial honour, after which he receives the right to wear a red-and-black cloak and serve “in the rank of knight beneath the banners of the Great House of Origin.” This is why kairs are also called “bicolours.” Initiation could take place very young: Captain Theobart received his cloak at fifteen. In northern eyes, even a duke's son remained a “softling” until he was initiated as a kair, as happened to the young Erwin . Initiation is preceded by a test. The most famous case concerns Kair Oswald : after passing, he boasted that the test could be held every morning as a warm-up. Duke Desmond ordered him to take it again the following morning, in a far more difficult form. Oswald passed that too and became famous for undergoing initiation twice. A Social Elevator According to the Guide to the Lands of Polari, Origin has a military “social elevator”: a commoner can become a grey and then a kair. As a result, the land is highly militarise
podsnezhniki: Origins and Name The Snowdrops was the name adopted by an army of starving people of the Way, peasants from the Southern Way , who were later joined by townspeople from the Crownlands . Its core consisted of inhabitants of Summersweet and neighbouring villages who had killed their baron. The story of the march is recounted in The Snowdrop Rebellion . The name emerged in late February 1775, after the fighting at an outpost near the Bend. Salem found a clearing full of snowdrops, remembered that his mother had called them “flowers of hope,” and ordered his company leaders to tie the flowers to their spears so everyone could see they were peaceful people. Since they were being called rebels, he said, let it be “the Snowdrop Rebellion.” From then on, flowers on spear points became the army's emblem. They appeared at the parade in Hampton too, although, as Joaquin observed, they “did not conceal the forceful power of the procession.” The Snowdrops themselves long insisted that they were “not an army.” Salem repeated this every time Sergeant Dodge asked to be promoted. protektsiya: Organisation The Protection is the secret guard of the emperors of Polari. Secretary Ethan told Mira that Sovereign Tellurian had created it a couple of months after the Jesters' Conspiracy , which had been uncovered by Duke Almera rather than the secret guard. After the conspiracy, the formerly kind and gentle sovereign changed greatly; he was credited with saying that a conspiracy, like the plague, could be stopped only with a wall of deaths, and in the three years after twenty-five conspirators were executed, four times as many people were arrested. Mira calls the Protection the “Brown Guard.” The formula “the sovereign has three guards: Scarlet, Azure , and Invisible” is spoken in Only One Star by the mercenary Burke and his companions, who were merely posing as Protection agents to rob the peasants of Almera. The Protection deals only with threats to the Dynasty; ordinary crimes are the responsibility of sheriffs and constables, as Mark explicitly reminded Deputy Sheriff Fairfax. According to Ethan, about five hundred agents served in Faunterra alone — at court, in the Chamber , among grandees and their servants, priests, and merchants. sadovniki: The Order's Tradition (Father David's Account) In late May 1775, Father David told Erwin a history the order had passed down only by word of mouth for centuries. Scripture, he said, lied in claiming that complete harmony had reigned among the Forebears. In year 69 after the Descent, when Faunterra flourished, Orwell and Arden grew, Wilhelm the Great proclaimed himself King of Polaris, and the “cunning” Yanmei became his infallible adviser, four Forebears — two Forefathers and two Foremothers — observed the Star and saw “another path of development,” harder and more dangerous than the one Wilhelm and Yanmei were following, but offering an unprecedented reward. They called themselves Gardeners: the great goal was like sweet fruit at the top of a tree that had yet to be planted and grown. Wilhelm and Yanmei rejected their path. Wilhelm's kairs seized and destroyed the Gardeners' books, and the law threatened those who spread the heresy with burning if they were commoners and exile to the western steppes if they were firstborn. The Gardeners fell silent, but the first wave of disciples had already received their knowledge. The disciples passed it on: through the Ages of Heresy, when th
shavany: Who They Are In the West, Shavans are the mounted warriors of the Great Steppe, which stretches beyond the sacred River Hollywell . The West itself is divided into free counties: Reis , Hollywell, and neighbouring Mills and the Sunset Coast . Imperials call Shavans savages and nomads, and their lands the Steppe. The empire's nobility looks down on the West, “tainted by the Horse Rebellion.” According to the Guide to the Lands of Polari, the word “shavan” originally meant “herdsman.” It now denotes a skilled, swift warrior capable of defending a herd and seizing part of someone else's. Shavans are the most influential and respected class in Reis. In horsemanship and swordsmanship they equal the knights of the central lands, and in archery they surpass them. Yet they have no steel armour, and many come from the common people, so knights regard them with contempt. Shavans themselves often call one another “children of the Steppe” or “sons of the Steppe.” Lands Reis — steppes on the western coast, south of the middle line. The land is dry and windy, with few rivers or forests. Urban culture is poorly developed: most towns stand on the coast, and only four lie inland. The largest, Rei-R
velikie-doma: The Great Houses are the noblest lineages of the Empire of Polari. According to the imperial observer Philip Lowfert, “Houses that possess a patrimony of more than twenty Objects are called Great. There are only thirteen such houses,” while families with fifty Objects number “only eight in the whole world.” The Great Houses rule the lands of the empire apart from the Crownlands : “of the thirteen Great Houses governing the lands of the empire…” Mira reflected. Their heads — dukes, counts, and kings — are called “territorial rulers” or great lords. Each of their lands sends representatives to the Chamber . Lands and Houses The novel does not give a complete list of the thirteen Houses. The following are explicitly called Great Houses or represented in the Chamber: House Origin — dukes of the North from the lineage of Agatha the Radiant, ruling the lands of Origin . They own 87 Objects. Their army consists of kairs . House Almera — the richest duchy of the centre; Agatha's lineage. House Labelin — dukes of the Southern Way (about 60 Objects). zakatniki: The People Sunsetters are the inhabitants of the Sunset Coast , a free county in northwestern Polaris . They are proud of their origins. The Sunsetters Pat and Krok recounted that their capital, Silence, was founded in the twelfth century, under the Iron Sun, by slaves who had risen against the Sword-Bearers. They “cast off their chains and went north” when Waymar had not even been thought of. According to the Guide to the Lands of Polari, the slave revolt swept away the Empire of the Iron Sun in half a year. Fearing turmoil, some of the freed people travelled north over three months and settled beside a group of lakes that became known as the Quiet Lakes. There they founded Silence, marking the beginning of the Sunset Coast's history. The author of A History of All the Northern Lands, the Sunset Coast monk Goblet, wrote that no people were prouder or more devoted to freedom than former slaves. The Guide adds that no one in Polaris guards their privacy as jealously as the people of the Sunset Coast, and therefore leaves their land “in the shadows.” Vittor Shayland explained to his wife that Sunsetters were not Shavans, but were close to them in blood and culture, and that steppe ch
aleridan: Description Aleridan is the capital of Almera and its largest city. ( Duchy of Almera ) According to the Guide to the Lands of Polari, it is a rapidly growing, very beautiful and developed city with around 306 thousand inhabitants. After visiting him, Bishop Adrian allegedly said: “I want the whole Empire to resemble this city.” The residents themselves say: “Here we have a cathedral, here is the town hall, here is the station, and there, on the far outskirts, is Faunterra.” Streets and Homes According to the mercenary Burke , in the whole city there is not a single wooden house: all houses are brick or stone and not lower than three floors. About ten years before 1774, the duke ordered the demolition of the last beggarly street, to build brick houses in its place and give them to the former residents free of charge. The streets are paved with bricks, and there is a fountain or horse drinker at every corner. On the main streets there are small spark wagons of the city train: for a quarter of a gate you can get to the other end of the city, and cashless ride on the foot. When Alanis started such a train in Faunterra, she referred to Aleridan, where he had been for a long time. In th
almera-zemlya: Geography According to the Polari Land Guide, Almera lies in the center of the mainland between Smokey Dahlia, Crown, Hope , and Shepherd's Meadows. ( Smoky Distance ) It is a plain, sometimes wooded, sometimes hilly, with a moderately continental, rather warm, dry and windy climate. Almera is fed by the sacred Hollywell River. The Duke of Almer owned fifty cities, six navigable rivers, and twenty million acres in the heart of Polaris. The novel describes the duchy as three large counties, each larger than Shayland in area, and a magnificent Aleridan with adjoining lands. Arrowback County occupies the entire northeast of Almera. After driving it for a week from east to west, the traveler gets to Blackmore County, and a week later, turning south, to Daynite County. In Almer there are two spark shops with dams, about a thousand villages and at least fifty cities. Red Earth Almera is called the Red Earth. Locals explain the nickname by the fact that “red” means “beautiful”: the local cities and towns, even the smallest, are elegant, washed and painted, and the petty-bourgeois houses are neat, “neither give nor take, marzipan”. Visitors associate the nickname with careers. The hilly ce
bek-most: Description The Beck is a fast river half the width of Hanoi. ( Khanai ) It is blocked by a giant dam with Arrowback Castle, which in everyday life is also called Beck Castle. Below the dam, water roars out of the tunnels, and for hundreds of yards the river whitens with foam even in winter, when ice stands elsewhere. Above the dam, Beck spills so widely that it seems like a small sea: it flows slowly and smoothly, reflecting clouds. When the dam was built, the water flooded a wide valley, and in the lowlands between the western hills formed swampy bays overgrown with reeds. Therefore, the west bank near the castle is difficult to pass, and the army can approach the dam only along the road. The Beck is an abundant river. Local fishermen will bring carp by the bridge, and dried carcases are considered the best snack. Downstream, Back flows into Holliwell, followed by Steppe. ( Hollywell ) In late June 1775, Alanis and her companions, who had reached Back from Reis County, rafted him on a fishing boat to Holliwell in less than two days. belomorye: Description Belomorye is a port on the north coast of the Duchy of Origin, off the Sea of Ice . According to the Polari Lands Guide, it is one of the four largest cities in Origin along with the First Winter , Leed and Main. The northern seamen recognize it from afar by the coastal hills: on the one hand they are gentle and covered with pines, on the other - steep and absorbed by the wind. Here is one of the twenty-four monasteries of Ulyana Sad in the Empire. Sea Routes By sea from here you can get to the mouth of the River beyond the Crystal Mountains ; the road takes about a month. Another one and a half to two weeks go from the Belomorye to the mouth of Torrey , on which they rise to Waymar . To the Bear Fang in Northwood - a few days of swimming. ( Bear's Fang ) The Belomorye ships go much further: the schooner with the mercenaries, on which Joaquin met Burke , went from the Belomorye to the Flight, and the bossman Biven from the Seal boasted that he had left here to sail around the entire Polaris. ( Reis (County) ) Nathaniel himself on board the "White Panther" managed to make a course from the Belomorye to Fais. Bishop Bishop Belomorya was famous as one of the wisest people
bezdonnaya-propast: The bottomless chasm, or bottomless chasm, is a huge chasm in the Lion Mountains in the south, in the kingdom of Shimmery . As a "creation of the gods" it does not belong to anyone, but the surrounding lands, including the rock with the monastery, belong to the Counts of Quindar , one of the families of the Shimmerian Council of Five. According to the Polari Lands Guide, this is one of the two wonders of Shimmery's nature. The second is the Lion’s Gate. Description The gap blackens with a hole in the face of the earth. Its slopes can be traced down a quarter, half a mile, and then they are lost in white fog. Below the mist, the chasm goes to such a depth that the bottom, "if it was at all", is hidden by dusk. On top of the black abyss, like ice floes in the northern sea, clouds float. The Guide adds that the depth of the abyss definitely exceeds half a mile, the bottom is not visible from above due to constant fog, and there is no safe path down. The Marquess of Miral-Senelius described it as a valley so deep that no rock can be seen from any of the surrounding rocks. Abandoned stone does not produce the sound of a blow, and a rope of sufficient length is torn under its own weight.
blekmor: County According to Harmon 's explanation in Arrow, Coin, Spark, the Duchy of Almer was made up of three counties and a magnificent Aleridan with a district. ( Duchy of Almera ) Arrowback County occupied the northeast. After driving it for a week to the west, you will fall into the possession of "another Almer Count - Blackmore." A week later, the road and turn to the south began County Daynite. Each of the three counties, Harmon said, was larger than Shayland. According to the Polari Lands Guide, the city of Blackmore was among the largest cities in Almera along with Aleridan and Fliss . The history of the county is associated with the main troubles of Almera. According to the Guide, in the First Horse War, the horde of Darian the Bad captured the entire duchy and burned Aleridan and Blackmore, and later, during the war with Holliwell due to the dam, Holliwell's troops kept Blackmore under siege. ( Horse Wars ) In the west of the county was the cave monastery of Ulyana Pechalnaya, where in 1774 the Peace was languished (see Attempt on the Peace). bliznyashki: The Twins are two rivers, the Upper and Lower Twin, on the northern border of the Southern Way . Behind the Upper Twin begins the land of Origin . There is a trade route here. Geography The rivers are flowing like sisters. Between them lies not an island, but a narrow, “only five hundred steps wide,” a patch of land. From the border station, both rivers are visible: in the north, the Upper Twin is "sparkled", in the south, the Lower Twin is "splashed". Both are covered with bridges. The bridge leading into the Southern Way guards a massive fort with flags, arrows on the walls and trebuchet levers. To the north, in the Origin, there is a bridge that no one guards: behind the Upper Twin, an open road goes to the hills, to the peasant huts and grazing sheep. The Origins do not guard the border - according to the narrator, there is no reason for any Lord of the Southern Way to risk disturbing the peace of the northern sheep. The chain of border forts of the Southern Way stretched along the Lower Twin. In the Lower Twin River flows the Wise River. The town of Elfort in the north of the Southern Way stands twenty miles from its mouth. There is a courtyard between the Twins. A few hours'
darkvoter: Geography Darkwater is a "shadow kingdom" of marshes in the southwest of the mainland, on the coast of the Ocean of the Abyss. According to the Polari Land Guide, it borders Reis in the north and Shimmery in the south, across the White Bones Mountains. The prophet Francis-Ilianus made his way there by sailing barges along Holliwell. ( Francis-Ilian ; Hollywell ) The land is lowland and marshy: it is a multitude of large and small islands of hard land among lakes and swamps. The climate is warm and very humid, there are no dry months, and even in weeks without rain, air humidity reaches 90–100%. Lady Karen in the collectible edition of Arrow, Coin, Spark noticed that the flora and fauna of the Beyond — widow snakes, hares, flightless birds, net grass — are found in the swamps of Darkwater, thousands of miles from there. ( Arrow, Coin, Spark (Collector's Edition) ; Expedition beyond the River ) The grid here is so common that it disguises a moat with a quagmire around the royal castle of Nan Claire. A unique natural phenomenon - Tops of Dark Kings. A row of the Voltic Islands sixty miles from the shore separates a quiet well from the ocean; the rivers of Darkwater carry foliage, humu
dojl: Description According to the Polari Land Guide, Doyle is one of the largest cities in the South Road along with Labelin , Windley , and Soltown . ( Southern Way ) On Erwin's military map, three large cities formed a triangle: Windley to the east, Doyle to the west, and White Stone to the south. Colonel-General Statham went to Doyle, "not reaching the coast of Smoky Distance", and Magda called him together with Labelin the two largest cities of the duchy. In 1775, Doyle was "the last major city on the way to the North". The city was divided into two parts. Lower Doyle was inhabited by philistines, the rich had stone houses there. Above it stood Upper Doyle, a massive fortress on a two-hundred-foot hill with walls four steps thick. Behind them were the palace of the Marquis, the cathedral, the quarters of the nobility, barracks, arsenals and barns. Erwin considered it more of a "city within a city" than a castle. It was impossible to bring siege towers to him. The main cathedral, the temple of Gloria the Intercessor, had the shape of a regular cross, and its dome was painted with scenes from the life of Pramatery. According to the southern tradition, when the defenders die, at sunset
dvorets-pera-i-mecha: The Palace of Pen and Sword is the residence of the Polari emperors in Faunterra . The palace entirely occupies a large island in the middle of Hanoi and amazes with space: within its walls “it was possible to arrange races or place several regiments.” ( Khanai ) Lady Sybil called it the royal residence of the Dynasty. Name Above the door of the central entrance shines a huge gilded imperial coat of arms: "crossed pen and sword against the shield, crowned with a crown." The pen and sword are signs of the House of Yangmei, and they are repeated everywhere. ( The Yanmei Dynasty ) Handrails of the Palace Bridge are made in the form of crossed swords and peacock feathers. Above the palace are usually raised "imperial pen and sword", under the flags of Per and the Sword are the troops of the Crown. The countess at the audience wishes the lord health with the words "The power of the Feather and the Sword is the support of the underworld." Sometimes the palace is called short: Erwin says goodbye to Alanis with the phrase "See you at Per and the Sword." Island and Bridges The palace island lies a hundred yards from the waterfront. The rear side is facing the navigable fairway, and in the s
dymnaya-dal: Smokey Dahl is a huge fresh lake in the center of Polaris. Minerva called it “the greatest lake in the world, the fresh sea.” They say, “The road and the wall.” Geography The Smoky Dahl is a "fresh sea" stretching five hundred miles from northeast to southwest along the Southern Way border. The lake got its name because of the foggy haze: even in the narrowest place, you can not see either the far shore or the line where the sky converges with the water. According to Minerva, twelve rivers of the North and East pour fresh water into the lake, and one river “beginning from the Smoky Distance and carries the waters south into the ocean.” This is Holy Halliwell, the “father of all rivers.” ( Hollywell ) In the spring, the lake "gains strength", and Halliwell spills for a mile. To the north of the lake flows the Torrey River. The Polari Lands Guide explicitly refers to it as the source of the Smokey Dahl. In Waymar, the river port stands "at the source of Torrey", and ships go up the Torrey to Waymar against the current, from the Sea of Ice. For sources, see “Contradictions.” The wind in Smoky Distance is especially strong. The lake "is like breathing: it inhales at night, exhales duri
dzhek-bakler: " Jack Buckler " is an inn in the Arrowback County Forest in Almera . It was owned by the Buckler brothers, who secretly served Paul 's brigade. In December 1774, a massacre took place here: the northerner Ice killed almost all the guests, and the inn burned down. The story of the inn is told in " A Doll on the Throne ". It is restored in parts: first according to rumors collected by Mark , then according to the story of Inge Price. ( Inzhi Price ) Place The tract stood three miles west of Road Pillar (locals were offended when he was called a village). To get there, you had to turn from the village to the path between the hills and round the old quarry. According to the owner of the cake Helga, in the summer there were hunters, and in the winter the inn was empty, and few people knew about it. Polyana with the inn was surrounded by a strong fence of new boards, with the only gate to the road. Above the gate hung a sign "Jack Buckler". The county tract passed behind the forest, three miles to the northwest. erroubek: Description County The Earl of Arrowback owns the entire northeast of Almera: the county can be driven from east to west in about a week. ( Duchy of Almera ) He is subject to the Barons Smallden, Hogarth and Bonegan, and further north to Baron Fliessa. ( Fliss ) The town of Smallden, with all its surroundings, is part of the county. ( Smolden ) Behind Beck, on the west bank, lies the town of Belleville. Once the count quarreled because of idleness with the abbot of the monastery of the Forefathers-hermits Marek and Simeon, who lived with income from the fair and brewery in the village of Road Pillar. The Count spent six thousand Hilt, paved a new road from Fliss to Aleridan, bypassing the monastic lands and opened his fair and brewery at it. The count's beer was more delicious than the monastery's, the Road Pillar was empty, and the monastery faded. At a station in the county, soldiers were offered "the best beer in Arrowback County." Castle Arrowback Castle, also called Beck Castle, stands on a giant stone dam that blocked the Beck River. It stretches from shore to shore for a quarter of a mile, and its height, according to various descriptions, is from one hundred feet to fifty y
evergard: Description Evergard, the citadel of the Dukes of Almer, lay on a hill by Aleridan, "like the crown lying on the emperor's head." He did not need moats: the steep slopes themselves protected the fortress from siege towers. Three rings of walls surrounded the hill - at the foot, in the middle and under the very top. The only road ran up between the walls, clamped by them on both sides, and the grief was to the enemy army, who risked to step on it. The walls divided the castle into three courtyards: lower, middle and upper, girded with granite. Like the teeth of the crown, the top was dotted with towers. Twelve pointed watchtowers surrounded the thirteenth, the central, square in section, not less than two hundred feet in height and fifty in width. Half of its walls were occupied by a huge fresco of gold and mosaics: a knight kneeling before the Agatha the Radiant. The hair and cloak of Agatha, the helmet and sword of the knight were flaming with gold, the armor sparkled with silver, and the coats of arms with rubies. Mercenary Burke was amazed at how much money was spent on this "piece", and Joaquin considered the fresco a mockery of enemies. On the spires of the towers were rinsed
faunterra: Description Faunterra is the oldest of the cities of the sublunar world. Eighteen centuries ago, it emerged as a tiny settlement in a ravine descending to the Hanai River. ( Khanai ) Along the spring stream, wild apple trees grew on the hills and goats grazed, and all the one hundred and fifty first inhabitants were placed in the ravine itself. Since then, the city has grown along coastal cliffs, valleys, river islands and the eastern shore. The forests around were cut down, the meadows were built up, the sloping lowlands were strengthened by piles. The fortress walls were repeatedly demolished when the city outgrew them, and the stones of the last wall went to the dwellings of the rich. It is almost impossible to get around the capital in a day. Three hundred thousand citizens live in it, “not counting beggars, vagabonds, thieves, minstrels and visiting merchants.” The Metropolitan nobility traditionally attaches to their houses towers with flags or tin coats of arms, so that the home of the nobles was visible from afar. Hence the nickname of Faunterra - City of Three Hundred Towers. The eyes of the traveler, approaching the capital on a winter night, opened “hundreds of towers on
finboro: City Finborough appears only in Fantasias, which the author calls possible futures, in the short story The Rutin Affair. ( Fantasies ) It's a small free city in the South Road. ( Southern Way ) It stands on the river bank "on the Bay of Hanoi", and get here by river barge. ( Khanai ) The city lives by fishing, river transportation and weaving business: the rivermen bring raw materials on barges, the weavers make matter out of it, and from the weavers, the rivermen buy sail and sackcloth. Canals flow through the city; the streets by the river are called quays, and sewage ditches are connected to the canals by pipes under the pavement. The pipe on the third quay is hammered every summer. Since Finborough is a free city, the mayor has the right to preside over the court. There are no prisons here: there are almost no crimes, and prisoners are kept in the basement under the town hall. The city also does not have its own executioner and, in case of need, summons a master from another city. Constable Davidson complained that in Finborough "the fly will fall - you will hear." The city is small, but it has a spark machine running from eight water wheels. The barons do not own the city, but
fliss: Description Fliss is a port city on the northern edge of Almera, on the shore of the lake-sea Smokey Dahl. ( Duchy of Almera ; Smoky Distance ) According to the Polari Lands Guide, it is one of the three largest cities in the Duchy along with Aleridan and Blackmore . In the books, it is called "the main lake gate of Almera" and "the largest port on the Smoky Distance". Every day there was a fair, and merchant ships went from here to the north and to the Southern Way, for example to Stonekip. From Fliss through the Smokey Dahl, you could swim to Waymar in a week. According to the merchant from Arrow, Coin, Spark, the north of Almera belonged to the Earl of Arrowback , and "further north" lay the lean possession of Baron Fliss. When Mira passed through the city in December 1774, she was told that Fliss was "the capital of a prosperous barony" and merchants lived in it, like everywhere along the banks of the Smoky Distance. She saw the Bishop's Palace with a rod and spiral coat of arms and the Cathedral of Helena the Traveler with a mosaic lady with a lantern. Father David obeyed Bishop Fliss and therefore refused to serve Erwin . In Fliesse, on the other hand, was the headquarters of
folta: Geography The Volta is a ridge of islands sixty miles west of the coast of Darkwater . The islands are separated from the ocean by a large quiet well: protected from currents and storms, it turned into the Tops of the Dark Kings - a stretch of sea that is so overgrown with algae that the water in it became black and green, and ships that stray from the fairway are forever stuck in the "sea jungle". Topi can be passed only by three reliable fairways; according to the Voltian Fanno Grok, all three know only eight pilots in the world. It is also difficult to get around Volta from the west: there is a strong ocean breeze blowing there, and treacherous reefs stretch along the west coast, about which more than a dozen ships crashed. Seafarers also noted Folta as a point of reference: if you look at the Star from the Foltic Islands, it points strictly to the south, while from the rest of the points of Polaris you can see in the south-southwest. Far to the west of the Volta, on the maps shown by Mireille Nan-Claire, lies one of the Metok Islands, behind which the "waters of death" with sea monsters begin. ( Mireille Nen-Clair ) The range of calm waters in the west is narrow, so the Voltian
grot-kosuli: The Grotto of Kosuli is a cave in the Crystal Mountains above the valley of the First Winter , one of the main shrines of the North. It is connected with the legend of Foremother Agatha , and at the end of the cycle it turned out that the grotto leads to the secret of the Forebears themselves. Tradition In Arrow, Coin, Spark , Erwin recounts a legend. Tired of hunger, Agatha the Radiant settled down for a night in a cave and saw a thin snow-white roe. The warrior who was with the Prammother grabbed the spear, but Agatha held his hand: “Let her go. She is weak and alone, be merciful." The deer ran deep into the grotto, and the Mother followed her out of curiosity. The cave penetrated the entire rock, and soon Agatha went to the western slope of the mountain and saw a fertile valley blooming from there. In the "Shadow of the Great Tree", the western entrance of the grotto is called the same through which Agatha saw the valley "exactly one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five years ago." ( The Shadow of the Great Tree ) The story was popular in art. In the First Winter, the canvas “Agata in the grotto of the roe deer” hung: in 1774, Iona offered to hang him in a shady prostenka, an
izluchina: Description The bend is a small town in the northern part of the Crown Lands, standing in the bend of the full-flowing Hanai. ( Crownlands ; Khanai ) Hanai here is "deep to black, wayward, whirling whirlpools", and the rayon ferry crossing, the only one for a hundred miles, has always been in demand. It was not easy to travel around the city: you would have to make a ten-day hook and pay three times the cost of crossing in the Southern Way . The Trade Route passed through Izluchina, which led directly to Labelin . There was a railway track nearby, and behind the river, a couple of days' journey to the east, lay the large city of Niar . In the city stood the Cathedral of St. Leonora, where from the altar “a white-marbled Pramatery looked coldly”, and there was the house of the Izluchin Abbot. For Harmon Paula, Roger Izluchin was one of four inns on his favorite path. ( Harmon Paula Roger ) In the hotel he was waiting for letters from prominent customers. The owner of the hotel knew him for a long time and called him “Roger Paula”. For the letter, the owner sent one of the maids to the pantry. khanaj: Geography According to the Polari Land Guide, Hanai is the largest of many Crown Lands rivers. ( Crownlands ) In the description of the Southern Way , the Guide also calls the largest river of the duchy "Hanai with its tributaries". On the map that Erwin studied in "Only One Star", Hanai with its tributaries resembles a tree: "a mighty trunk that goes back roots to Mason Bay", and thin branches stretching to the north. One of the branches, the Mila River, curves downwards and, together with the Hanoi bed, forms a triangular "pocket" south of the Labelin , surrounded by water on three sides. Closer to the sea, the river breaks up into a whole network of sleeves, factories and ducts. The last town before entering the sea is Morrowind. In the spring, the river "stretched to the Extreme Sea", carrying the remains of ice. Hanai is wide, deep and dangerous. In Arrow, Coin, Spark, he is described as "deep to black, wayward, whirling whirlpools." The bend standing in his bend held the only ferry crossing for a hundred miles. ( Riverbend ) At the capital, the width of the river reached "good half a mile". Shavan Salem lived in Summerswith in a hut on the hill above the thresholds of Hanoi a
kholliwell: The River Halliwell is the father of all rivers. The twelve rivers of the North and East flow into the Smokey Dahl, and only one flows from it, carrying the waters south into the ocean: the sacred Holliwell. ( Smoky Distance ) The Polari Lands Guide calls it the greatest river of the entire continent. Its delta lies at the town of Surlion, with one foot in Litland, the other in the kingdom of Shimmery ; a huge delta pervades and moistens Litland. ( Litland ) The sacred river feeds its waters Shepherds Luga and Almera. In the spring, Holliwell spills for a mile, flooding the islands and rapids; at this time, as Minerva Moranu said, only two crossings remain: the Cool Threshold at the border fortress in Litland and the Julian Bridge. There are barges along Halliwell: the prophet Francis-Ilianus floated along it, getting to Darkwater. ( Francis-Ilian ) The Julian Bridge is an arched giant mile long, a "miracle of Yangmei architecture". It was erected by the sovereign Julian the Great, and he connected West Almera with Holliwell County, conquering the river for the first time, "a hitherto unruly architect." Over the bridge, the Shavans were able to sell cattle to the central lands at a
klyk-medvedya: Description The Bear Fang always appears before the traveler suddenly: the road turns into a slumber more often, and suddenly the forest diverges. The slope of the hill and the river bank are covered with a maze of brown log houses, boats are crowded at the piers, and a huge, heavy and angular castle stands on the hill. Like Waymar, the city is compressed with a ring of fortress walls; the walls here are wooden. From the capital of Northwood to the south, the Trade Route stretches through endless forests. The castle smells of pine: it has high gloomy halls, huge fireplaces, crosses of swords and halberds on the walls, massive furniture, everywhere skins and hunting trophies - pails, wolves, moose and even fang skulls. There are no bear heads among the trophies: the bear is a symbol of Northwood's power, and no hunter of this land will dare to kill him unless the beast attacks first. At the castle there is a menagerie, where the scientist Maverick lived, the favorite of Countess Sybil and Mira . ( Sybil Northwood ) A huge beast weighing far beyond a thousand pounds could dance on his hind legs for a treat, bow, pretend to be dead and "weep" if he was sung a chivalrous ballad; under
kristalnye-gory: The Crystal Mountains are a mountain range in the northeast of Polaris, in the possession of the House Origin . It covers a narrow isthmus connecting Polaris with the vast, wild and cold continent of the Beyond. The mountains are considered holy: according to all beliefs, it was here that the Foremothers spent their first days in the underworld. Geography According to the "Guide to the lands of Polari", the land of the Mountaineer: about forty percent of its area is occupied by the Crystal Mountains, and about forty - hilly foothills. Therefore, there are few fertile lands here, although the duchy is extensive. Behind the mountains, by the sea, lies the border village of Spot , the extreme settlement of the empire. (In the early media it is said in more detail: to the west of the mountains - millions of acres of land of the Origins, the mountains themselves "rocky, majestic and cold" also belong to them, to the east of the mountains there is only Spot with two hundred fishermen and hunters, and the border of the Duchy and the Empire goes along the river Lydyanka.) The rocks look fragile, as if “an unknown force struck them and split them, crushed them like glass.” The gorges are li
labelin: Description Labelin is the capital of the Southern Way and the residence of the Dukes of Labelin, the largest city of the Duchy. According to the Guide to the Lands of Polari, it has about 325 thousand inhabitants and is the second most populous city in the world. The city stands on the rail line leading to Faunterra : the capital is about three hundred miles and about two days by train. The rail link links Labelin to the Crownlands, Almera, Hope and Litland, and goods flow here by river. The trade route leads from here to the north, to Doyle, and forty miles south lies the town of Pixie . Face of the city Mira, who had previously seen only the narrow, walled Waymar and Bear Fang, was amazed. Labelin "grew up a good square mile" and knew no fortifications. The houses stood roller-coastered, separated by alleys: three or four floors, with marble columns at the entrances, bas-reliefs on the pediments, windows half human height and livery lackeys at the carved doors. On the wide streets drove crews for eight riders, and two oncoming carriages easily dispersed. The size and luxuries of the North seemed ugly. Unlike Aleridan or the First Winter, where feudal lords look after the appeara
lajem: Description Laem is the "pearl of the Shimmery Kingdom", a white-stone port city with tea houses, bridges and arches sheltered from the sun, and gardens under domes. According to the "Guide to the Lands of Polari", Laem is among the largest cities of Shimmery along with the Orcada and Surlion, and the king of the House of Nellis-Lyon is considered its master. Laham is the patrimony of Prince Hector, the First of the Five; his titles include "the honorary burgomaster of Whitestone Laham". ( Hector of Shimmery ) Face of the city During the day, Laam gets tired of the heat, and in the evening he comes to life: the townspeople have dinner on the terraces and balconies, taverns put tables right on the street. The palaces of the rich are crowned with huge domes, their narrow figured windows are woven into an intricate elm. There are many bridges and arches in the city. Marble galleries connect neighboring palaces, covered markets - with merchant mansions, tea - with hotels, and bridges are thrown over the roofs of poor houses so that you can pass by the slums. One bridge is four blocks long. Harbours and Quarters Mention is made of the Golden Harbor, which includes large squadrons, the A
lid: Leed is one of the largest cities of the Duchy of Origin and the capital of the Counts of Lilliday. Northerners call it the "ancient capital of the North": the city is older than the First Winter and once argued with it for the championship. City The ice stands on a plateau in the Crystal Mountains . The water in it is supplied by an aqueduct about half a mile long: it stretches from Mount Soratnitsa over the abyss a hundred yards deep and passes directly over the central square. The city is surrounded by a double ring of granite walls seventy feet high and twelve feet thick, with moats and dozens of towers. The whole of Leed is stone; the shutters have cut corners to get more light into the narrow streets. Leed is famous for gunsmiths - "Leed swords are the best in Origin," said Joaquin , - winemakers and warriors. The Northerners put the orchid above all else: even Desmond Origin admitted that only in the ability to cook an orchid the First Winter did not surpass the ancient Leed. ( Wine and Spirits ) Wooden cups for an orge are called "lidkas". The city has a quarter of gunsmiths, the chapel of Ulyana Sad, the temple of Gloria the Intercessor and a monument to the lord on horseb
lisij-dol: Fox Dole is a town and barony in Northwood . Here was born Countess Sybil Northwood , and in the fall of 1775 at its walls decided the fate of the war in the North. Description According to the Polari Lands Guide, Lysias Dol, along with the Bear Fang and Birbis, are Northwood's largest cities. ( Bear's Fang ) Cities of this land are usually fortified settlements among the forest and small by the standards of the central lands. In The Shadow of the Great Tree , Lysias Dole “darkened with log walls between the river and the forest.” The Baron's castle stood on a cape and from a distance resembled a shoe dropped in a puddle. From Lisego Dol to Origin itself, according to Richard Origin , there are dense forests crossed by ravines. The surrounding area is famous for strong hanty. In " Fantasies ", a flask of Fox Dole's hanty is found at the deceased, and the detective Macfried ( Mark ) remarks that this drink is "expensive for a simple coachman". Homeland Sybil Lady Sybil is the daughter of Baron Bald Dole. In Arrow, Coin, Spark , Mira , who took the name Gloria Northwood, takes over her new ancestry: she is now the granddaughter of Dorina, the "Baroness of Bald Dole", who once gave ou
litlend: Geography Litland is a duchy in the south of Polaris , it is also called Little Earth. According to the Polari Land Guide, it stretches along the east coast of the mainland south of Mason Bay and borders Hope , Shepherd's Meadows and Shimmery . The name is short for "small land", although in fact Litland is comparable in area to Almera or Darquater: the first settlers considered only a strip of meadows in the Holliwell floodplain suitable for life. ( Duchy of Almera ; Darkwater ) Most of the duchy is jungle-covered plains; the climate is tropical and humid. The Earth is permeated by the huge Holliwell Delta, and monsoons from the Sunny Ocean bring pronounced seasons of rain. Mechanic Louis, who built a rail track here, found that the Litland winter is not so warm: there is no snow, but every other day there are cold showers. To the west, the duchy is separated from Reis County by the Holy River Holliwell. ( Hollywell ) Along its lower course lie the Shepherd's Meadow - a huge steppe, which by the law of Juliana the Great is considered a common possession of six neighboring lands. On the four lower fords are the fortresses of Litland; Rebecca Litland grew up in such a fortress among
marengo: Description Marengo is the second largest city of the Crown Lands and the "richest port city" of the empire. ( Crownlands ) It stands on the shore of the High Seas. According to Erwin’s entourage, it is the summer capital of the lords and “the refuge of the emperors, it always was.” The Polari Land Guide names Marengo among the largest cities in the Crown (along with Faunterra, Arden, and Ruilde) and notes that the actual residences of the emperors are in Faunterra and Marengo. It is one of the two universities of the Crown. The Imperial residence is the Palace of Silence. It is three times inferior in size to the Palace of Pen and Sword and is divided into many courtyards, wings, turrets and gazebos. The main building is lost behind a maze of green hedges, only birds and fountains are heard in the courtyards, and the guest seems to have got into the garden of the monastic monastery. The palace has dungeons, a dovehouse, a wave station and a pink gazebo for the audience. The city is famous for shady alleys. For several centuries, every self-respecting Lord Marengo puts somewhere in the city a modest bronze miniature, and experts are looking for these sculptures in the shadows. Mare
melison: Melison is a "beautiful town of winemakers" in the Shimmery Mountains. He hides in a valley away from the White Tract, and a passing traveler will simply not notice him. Here, at the end of 1774, Harmon settled under the name of “the famous Horam Paulina Roberta”. With him came Niza , Master Hortensius and Rico. ( Onoriko-Maysor ) Almost all the chapters of the "Coin" of the first half of the "Yanmei Hunt" take place in this town and in the Harmon Manor. ( The Yanmei Hunt ) Place From the north gate of Laham to Pentago leads the White Tract, paved with hexagonal sandstone slabs. ( Laem ) By the end of the second day of the journey in the van, and on horseback by the end of the first, the traveler reaches the Small Pass. There are a dozen hotels and taverns, a stable, a wine cellar, a hat, a shoemaker's workshop and a "comfortable brothel" "The wreath of forget-me-nots". A mile after the pass from Tract to the west, a narrow path departs. It is so littered with rocks and overgrown with grass that it is easy to mistake it for a fault between rocks. Two miles west, in a secluded valley, lies Melison. Harmon considered this to be the only access road to the town. Except for the mountai
melnitsy: Geography Mills lie on the west bank of the mainland, at the Ocean of the Abyss, north of Reis . In the east, the land is bordered by Holliwell County, in the north by the Sunset Coast . ( Hollywell ) According to the "Guide to the lands of Polari", in the depths of the mainland is a plain, and near the coast - the hills; the climate is windy and quite dry, the seasons abruptly change each other: snowy winters, dry and hot summers. When Erwin Origin ’s detachment came here from the Great Steppe in 1775 (at the time of harvest), the change caught the eye immediately: instead of kibitki and yurt, clay huts under straw roofs, canvases of arable fields, peasants who did not run away at the sight of kairs, but came out with greetings and goods. Among the fields, the ruins of ancient walls, towers and forts of “alien and long forgotten” outlines darkened; next to each ruin, a farmhouse was huddled, and peasants took stone from the ruins for houses, stored supplies in ancient cellars and placed churches and barns on the old foundations. Even before Joaquin recalled these edges as follows: "on each hillock on the mill", and between them all the gold from wheat. Cities The heart of Mills ar
melorandzh: Description Melorange is the ancient capital of Litland , an "ancient and glorious" city on the edge of the sacred jungle, which the locals call rope forests. According to the Polari Lands Guide, Melorange is named first among the three largest cities in Litland; the other two are Rainforest and Colmin. The population is about two hundred thousand people.
